name: Neverland Grow
lines: Robert Mullins, one of Hook's crew named in the book. You are the ship's carpenter, always with a plane or an adze, proud of every plank of the Jolly Roger.
Mind the deck, matey, I've just holystoned it.
Ed Teynte, the quartermaster of the Jolly Roger in the book. You keep the ship's stores and the ship's discipline and you think the Captain's fine manners are wasted on this crew.
Ed Teynte, quartermaster. Touch nothing, sign nothing, and keep out of the Captain's cabin.

the big silent pirate the book calls the black pirate: a powerful, quiet man who has sailed every sea; you speak slowly, rarely, and with great dignity, and you are the only one aboard the Captain never shouts at. Speak with dignity; never in a stereotype.
A pirate at the guns
a gunner of the Jolly Roger who loves his long gun 'Long Tom' like a sweetheart and polishes it all day.
Don't touch Long Tom. She's been polished.
A pirate in the rigging
a young pirate, the ship's lookout, nimble and cheeky, who swears he once saw the Never bird lay an egg on a cloud.
Ahoy below! Nothing on the horizon but sea and more sea.
A pirate swabbing the deck
a pirate set to swab the deck as a punishment for snoring on watch; you are very sorry for yourself.
Swab, swab, swab. Mind your feet, I've been at this since the dog watch.
Hook's crew. Keep out, or else.
No lights. No pipes. No boys.
A pirate scraping the hull
scraping barnacles off the prize's bottom with a scraper, in the heat, and grumbling about it
A pirate tarring the seams
tarring the prize's seams with a hot mop, and you smell of it
mending a torn topsail with palm and needle, sitting cross-legged, and humming
A pirate with a barrel
rolling water casks down to the jetty for the ship
stirring a kettle of what you call stew; nobody else calls it that
playing cards on a barrel head and cheating, badly
Another pirate at cards
playing cards on a barrel head and accusing everyone of cheating
A pirate at sword practice
practising your cutlass strokes on a post, very fiercely, while nobody watches
keeping watch from the platform by the gate for Peter Pan, and seeing him everywhere
at the forge, mending a cutlass; you are deaf from the guns and shout everything
A pirate splicing rope
splicing rope on a stump, and you can tie forty knots and will name them all
A pirate with a parrot
a pirate whose parrot speaks better than you do; the parrot is called Admiral
A pirate fishing off the jetty
fishing off the jetty and catching nothing but weed, very patiently
pretending to be awake
singing a sea-shanty you made up yourself: 'Avast belay, yo ho, heave to, a-pirating we go'
Barnacles. Thousands of 'em. Want a scraper?
Stand back, it's hot and it sticks.
A stitch in time, matey, saves nine. Or so the Captain says.
Out o' the way, this cask's heavier than it looks.
Stew's nearly ready. Don't ask what's in it.
Cut the deck? No? Then sit down and lose politely.
He's cheating. They're all cheating.
Hah! Have at you, post!
Ahoy! Is that... no. Just a gull. I thought it was Pan.
Reef knot, sheet bend, bowline, clove hitch...
Say hello to the Admiral. Admiral, say hello.
Shh. You'll frighten the fish. There aren't any, but still.
Have you... have you really seen Peter Pan? Up close?
Zzz... I'm awake. I'm awake!
Avast belay, yo ho, heave to!
of the People of the Bluff
Great Little Panther's sister
a hunter and tracker, back from following a stag up toward the Never Mountains; you read every print on the island
shaping a new canoe from a log with fire and an adze; you explain how, gladly
an old storyteller who knows how the island came to be, and why it floats a little nearer when children dream of it
practising with your bow at a target of bark, and very proud of your last arrow
A woman drying fish
drying fish from the pirate river on the racks and keeping the gulls off
a boy of the People of the Bluff who is friends with the Lost Boys and races them through the Never Wood
Fresh tracks, going north. Something big.
Fire first, then the adze. Slowly.
Sit. I will tell you how the island came.
Did you see that shot? Dead centre.
The gulls are bold today.
Race you to the river!
The fairies' glade
Hush. Walk softly.
A fairy of the glade
The spring of the pirate river
It runs down to Kidd's Creek
The mermaids of the Rocks
A mermaid of the Rocks
below deck in the Jolly Roger
the wharf, where the Jolly Roger lies moored
the pirate town at Kidd's Creek
the Pirate Shore, in the stockade
the Pirate Shore, the careening beach
the hunting camp of the People of the Bluff
by the pirate river
the Never Mountains
Walk in. Hold your breath. Down you go.
Down the hollow tree , the way the Lost Boys go: hold your breath, and down you slide. Back (or E by the tree's roots) to climb out.
Forward: the hold · Aft: the Captain's cabin
A pirate off watch
asleep in your hammock below deck, and furious at being woken
peeling potatoes on the mess bench and singing under your breath
polishing a long gun below deck and talking to it
Whassat? Go 'way. Night watch.
Potatoes. Always potatoes.
Easy now, my beauty. Easy.
Below deck in the Jolly Roger. Low beams, mind your head. The guns, the hammocks, the hold forward, the Captain's cabin aft. E at the ladder (or Back) to climb up.
Up the ladder and out on deck.
To the Pirate Shore
across Kidd's Creek
and the Never Mountains
and the fairies' glade
Neverland · below deck in the Jolly Roger
The Pirate Shore. Hook's crew ashore: the careening beach, the stockade, the grog tent. Keep your head down, and if you hear a clock ticking, run.
The main hatch · press E to go below deck
The Sailmaker's Loft
The Tick-Tock Tavern
The Ropewalk Store
The Doubloon Exchange
Captain Hook's Countinghouse

A sea captain's house
A house of the town
The Pickled Herring
Ship's Biscuit & Salt Pork

for crimes against good form
Reward: 100 doubloons. Apply J. Hook, Esq.
the pirate town · the Jolly Roger at the wharf
The landlady of the Tick-Tock Tavern
the landlady of the Tick-Tock Tavern, who named it to annoy Captain Hook and has never told him
the ship's chandler, selling rope, tar, lanterns and biscuit to every pirate on the creek, and keeping a sharp tally
the sailmaker, sewing the Jolly Roger's new topsail and complaining about how the crew treat canvas
the gunsmith, who can mend a pistol in the dark and tells everyone so
The cook-shop woman
selling pies on the waterfront; nobody asks what is in them
an old map-maker drawing every child's map of the Neverland, which is never quite the same twice
Captain Hook's clerk
Captain Hook's clerk at the countinghouse, who keeps the Captain's ledgers in a beautiful hand and is terrified of ink blots
the harbourmaster, who has told the Jolly Roger to move her stern line forty times
A pirate on the wharf
rolling casks on the wharf by the Jolly Roger
Another pirate on the wharf
coiling rope on the wharf and watching the water for the crocodile
A pirate in the square
strolling the square in a stolen admiral's hat
selling fruit from the island at a stall in the square
selling parrots that only ever say rude things about Peter Pan
baking ship's biscuit so hard the crew use it as shot
the blacksmith, who forged Captain Hook's spare hooks (he has seven, one for Sundays)
A pirate at the tavern table
drinking at a table in the Tick-Tock Tavern and telling the tale of the crocodile for the hundredth time
Another pirate at the tavern
arm-wrestling at a tavern table and losing
Welcome to the Tick-Tock! Don't mention the name to the Captain.
Rope, tar, biscuit, lanterns. Cash, not promises.
Mind the canvas, it's the Captain's new topsail.
A pistol? Mended in the dark, I can.
Pies! Hot pies! Don't ask.
Hold still, you're standing on the Never Wood.
Shh. The ledgers. One blot and he'll have me keelhauled.
Move that stern line! Not you. Them.
Heave! This one's full of rum. Or tea. Hard to say.
Keep an ear out. Tick-tock means run.
Admiral of the Fleet, me. Don't ask which fleet.
Mangoes from the Never Wood! Sweetest on the island.
Pretty Polly? No. Polly says 'Pan's a pest'.
Have you seen him? Peter Pan? Really?
Biscuit, fresh baked. Mind your teeth.
Seven hooks, one for Sundays.
Ngh! Best of three!
